q.t: Which of these can you use to measure the length of a table?
q.e: A handspan is a length — you see how many fit along the table.

q.t: Leena and Adi each measure the same table with their handspans and get different answers. Why?
q.e: A bigger hand fits fewer times along the same table.

q.t: Shopkeepers measure cloth with a:
q.e: A metre rod is the same length everywhere, so everyone gets a fair amount.

q.t: A one-metre rope is folded in half. Each half is:
q.e: Folding in half makes 2 equal parts of the metre.

q.t: That half-metre piece is folded in half again. Each part is now:
q.e: Half of a half is a quarter: the metre is now in 4 equal parts.

q.t: How many half metres make 1 metre?
q.e: Two equal halves make the whole metre.

q.t: How many quarter metres make 1 metre?
q.e: Folding a metre in half twice gives 4 equal quarters.

q.t: Which is most likely longer than 1 metre?
o: the height of a classroom door
q.e: A door is taller than a grown-up, which is much more than a metre.

q.t: Which is most likely shorter than 1 metre?
q.e: A pencil fits in your hand; a metre is about as long as a big step.

q.t: How can you check if a big table will fit through the door without lifting it?
o: Measure both with a thread and compare
q.e: A thread can carry the table’s length to the door so you can compare the two.

q.t: How many half metres are there in 3 metres?
q.e: Each metre has 2 half metres: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

q.t: How many quarter metres are there in 2 metres?
q.e: Each metre has 4 quarters: 4 + 4 = 8.

q.t: How many cuts do you make to cut a rope into 4 pieces?
q.e: Each cut makes one more piece. 1 piece → 2 → 3 → 4 needs 3 cuts.

q.t: Two half-metre ribbons and one 1-metre ribbon are joined. How long is the ribbon now?
q.e: Two halves make 1 metre, and 1 metre more makes 2 metres.

q.t: A table is 4 pencils long. A paper strip is as long as 2 pencils. How many strips long is the table?
q.e: Each strip covers 2 pencil lengths, so 4 pencil lengths need 2 strips.

q.t: Which is the shortest?
q.e: A quarter is 1 of 4 equal parts of a metre — smaller than a half.

q.t: A ribbon is 1 metre long. A quarter metre is cut off. How much is left?
q.e: 4 quarters − 1 quarter = 3 quarters.

q.t: Adi’s footstep is longer than Leena’s. Both walk across the same room. Who takes fewer steps?
q.e: Longer steps cover more ground each time, so fewer of them are needed.

q.t: A 1-metre mark is drawn on the wall. Ravi’s head is above it and Sita’s head is below it. Who is taller than 1 metre?
q.e: Ravi reaches past the 1-metre mark, so he is more than 1 metre tall.

q.t: Which unit gives the same answer for everyone who measures?
q.e: Hands, feet and arms differ from person to person, but a metre is always the same length.

q.t: How many cuts do you make to cut a rope into 6 pieces?
q.e: Each cut adds one piece, so you need one cut fewer than the number of pieces: 6 − 1 = 5.

q.t: Half a metre and a quarter metre joined together make:
q.e: Half a metre is 2 quarters; add 1 more quarter to get 3 quarters.

q.t: How many quarter-metre pieces can you cut from 3 metres of rope?
q.e: Each metre gives 4 quarters: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.

q.t: A table is 8 of Adi’s handspans long and 10 of Leena’s. Whose handspan is longer?
q.e: Fewer handspans fit along the same table, so each of Adi’s must be longer.

q.t: 4 half-metre strips are laid end to end. How long are they together?
q.e: Every 2 half metres make 1 metre, so 4 half metres make 2 metres.

q.t: A table is longer than the door is wide, but the table’s breadth is shorter than the door’s width. Can it go through?
o: Yes, if you turn it so the short side goes first
Only if you lift it over the roof
q.e: What has to fit is the side that faces the door; the short side fits.

q.t: A paper strip is half a metre long. How many strips make 2 metres?
q.e: 2 strips make 1 metre, so 2 metres need 2 + 2 = 4 strips.

q.t: What is the best tool to measure the length of a playground?
q.e: A long, standard rope needs fewer moves and gives a fair answer; a pencil would take ages.

q.t: Shelly’s string is longer than Adi’s. Adi’s string is longer than Leena’s. Whose string is the shortest?
q.e: Shelly’s > Adi’s > Leena’s, so Leena’s is at the short end.

q.t: Ravi jumps 1 metre. Sita jumps half a metre more than Ravi. How many half metres does Sita jump?
q.e: 1 metre is 2 half metres; one more half makes 3 half metres.

q.t: A saree is 5 metres long. Two curtains are cut from it, each 2 metres long. How much saree is left?
q.e: The curtains use 2 + 2 = 4 metres. 5 − 4 = 1 metre.

q.t: A 3-metre rope is cut into quarter-metre pieces. How many cuts are made?
q.e: 3 metres make 12 quarter pieces, and 12 pieces need one cut fewer: 11 cuts.

q.t: To decorate a board’s border, each long side needs 3 paper strips and each short side needs 2. How many strips for the whole border?
q.e: A board has 2 long and 2 short sides: 3 + 2 + 3 + 2 = 10.

q.t: Chetan jumps 1 metre. Ben jumps a quarter metre. How many of Ben’s jumps make one of Chetan’s?
q.e: 4 quarter metres make 1 metre.

q.t: Asha joins 3 half-metre ribbons and 2 quarter-metre ribbons end to end. How long is it?
q.e: 3 halves = 1 metre and a half. 2 quarters = another half. Together: 2 metres.

q.t: Which is the same length as one metre?
q.e: 2 halves make a whole metre. 3 quarters is less, and 2 quarters is only a half.

q.t: Tara is 1 metre and a quarter tall. Raj is half a metre shorter than Tara. How tall is Raj?
q.e: 1 metre and a quarter is 5 quarters. Half a metre is 2 quarters. 5 − 2 = 3 quarters.

q.t: A toy bridge is 1 metre tall. Three boxes, each half a metre tall, are stacked. Can the stack go under the bridge?
o: No, the stack is taller than the bridge
Yes, they are exactly the same height
q.e: 3 half metres is 1 metre and a half, which is more than 1 metre.

q.t: A 2-metre ribbon: half a metre goes to Asha and a quarter metre goes to Ben. How many quarter metres are left?
q.e: 2 metres = 8 quarters. Asha takes 2 quarters and Ben takes 1: 8 − 3 = 5.

q.t: There are 4 strings of lights 1 metre long and 4 strings half a metre long. How many metres of lights in all?
q.e: 4 one-metre strings = 4 metres. 4 half metres = 2 metres. 4 + 2 = 6.
